item.title: Seto: The Pottery Town That Named Japan's Ceramics — Guide
item.description: Seto, in the hills east of Nagoya, has fired ceramics for some 1,300 years — so long and so centrally that ‘setomono’, literally ‘things from Seto’, became the everyday Japanese word for pottery itself. The town wears its trade openly: alley walls are built from stacked kiln bricks and discarded tools, shrine guardians and even bridge railings are ceramic, and along the Kamagaki-no-Komichi kiln-wall path the workshops of working potters open for browsing.
